$comment: Contract expectations for the DOKIPON commerce deployment. Derived from contracts/openapi.yaml (the contract of record). The audit checks the live deployment against these, so a server that drifts from the contract fails here rather than in a user's browser. Where the contract documents a limitation, the expectation encodes that limitation rather than an idealised behaviour — an expectation that is wrong makes the audit lie.

paths.note: the edge's own health check. It answers 200 with an empty body: it is not a JSON endpoint, and contracts/openapi.yaml does not describe it.
Storefront schema: all four are required

Session schema. `sessionId` is camelCase in the contract while the rest of the session is snake_case (`expires_at_ms`), so it is checked field by field. This entry is here because the response used to carry `session_id`: the Dart client reads `json['sessionId']` only, so every guest session arrived with an empty id and 'add to cart' did nothing — while the response was still 200 with the right number of fields.
ProductPage: items is required and must not be empty for a seeded catalogue
the channel filter is a server responsibility; the line channel may legitimately have fewer products
orders are scoped to the buyer, so a request without a session must be refused, not served. 401 is the correct answer here — an audit that expected 200 would have called correct behaviour a defect.

the inventory service exposes only the three reservation write routes; contracts/openapi.yaml records this as x-blocked-by: inventory-service-has-no-list-route on /admin/v1/inventory. This expectation flips to 200 when the listing route lands — that is the point of having it here.
an unknown path must be a 404 from the edge, not a 500 and not a pass-through to whichever service happens to be last
the catalogue is read-only: a write to it must be refused, not silently accepted

adminPaths.note: the admin facade is authenticated; without a session it must refuse, not crash
same — the facade refuses before it even reaches the upstream

productDetail.$comment: ProductDetail is required to carry these camelCase names. A server that emits snake_case here is the exact defect the prototype documented: the Dart client reads camelCase only, so the field silently arrives empty.
